title: Cline vs Claude Code
summary: Cline vs Claude Code: developers deciding whether provider configuration is a core requirement.

sections.heading: Provider choice is an operating responsibility
paragraphs: For each candidate, write down the model endpoint, credentials owner and spending limit. A configurable provider helps only when someone can maintain and audit that configuration.

sections.heading: Local inference is a separate trial
paragraphs: A local client is not the same as local model inference. If offline operation is mandatory, verify the entire tool chain and run the same acceptance test without relying on cloud services; no offline guarantee is made here.

sections.heading: When neither is a fit
paragraphs: If your required security, data location or operating environment is not supported by current evidence, pause the purchase. Use the sources below to resolve the missing constraint before accepting a recommendation.

verdict: Evaluate Cline for provider choice, and Claude Code for its documented coding-agent workflow. Decide using the permitted account and execution environment.
bestFor: Developers deciding whether provider configuration is a core requirement
notFor: Users expecting a local client to guarantee local inference
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.

faqs.question: Which local model options does Cline document?
faqs.answer: Cline's current guide lists Ollama, LM Studio and Atomic Chat, with local-server configuration examples. This establishes documented configuration options, not model quality, hardware suitability or a fully offline workflow.

faqs.question: Do the two tools imply the same model billing route?
faqs.answer: No. Cline documents provider sign-in and bring-your-own-key configurations; Claude Code distinguishes subscription usage from API token billing. Compare the account and provider you will actually use.

faqs.question: When does Cline receive prompts or code?
faqs.answer: Cline's Privacy Notice says content using your own API key goes directly to the provider and is not collected by Cline. With Cline-provided keys, Cline says it collects content to facilitate requests to model providers. The provider's terms govern its handling; this does not verify a specific account or setting.

faqs.question: Does Claude Code's self-hosted environment support local inference like Cline's documented local models?
faqs.answer: Cline's current docs list Ollama, LM Studio and Atomic Chat as local model options. Anthropic's self-hosted Claude Code docs describe session runners on customer infrastructure but say inference still goes to api.anthropic.com; they do not document an on-device local-model route. No model or account configuration was tested.
